# CodeQL — GitHub's Semantic Code Analysis
<!-- Generated By: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.6) -->

Covers: CodeQL's capabilities, supported languages, and relevance to scanning
AI-generated code. See `../citations.md` for full source details.

---

## Overview

CodeQL is GitHub's semantic code analysis engine that lets you "query code as
though it were data" [11]. It powers GitHub Advanced Security and is used by
security researchers worldwide.

---

## Core Capabilities

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Supported Languages | C/C++, C#, Go, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, GitHub Actions [11] |
| Query Suites | Default (high precision, few false positives) and Security-Extended (broader coverage, more findings) [11] |
| Analysis Type | Semantic analysis, dataflow tracking, taint analysis |
| License | Open-source queries and libraries on GitHub [11] |

## AI-Powered Features

### Copilot Autofix (Beta March 2024) [11]

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Remediation rate | 2/3+ of found vulnerabilities [11] |
| Alert type coverage | 90%+ in supported languages (JS, TS, Java, Python) [11] |
| Resolution time with Autofix | 0.66 hours average [11] |
| Resolution time without Autofix | 1.29 hours average [11] |
| Scale | 460,000+ security alerts processed [11] |
| AI model used | OpenAI GPT-4 [11] |

### Incremental Analysis (September 2025) [11]

- Available for all CodeQL languages
- Only analyzes new or changed code
- Performance improvement: C# and C/C++ ~5% faster, Go ~20% faster, some scans 40%+ faster [11]

### Hybrid AI + CodeQL Model (March 2026) [11]

- AI-based scanning supplements CodeQL for broader language/framework coverage
- Extends to Shell/Bash, Dockerfiles, Terraform, PHP, and other ecosystems
- Operates at PR level — selects appropriate tool (CodeQL or AI) per case
- Internal testing: 170,000 findings over 30 days, 80% positive developer feedback [11]
- Expected public preview early Q2 2026

## Relevance to AI-Generated Code

### Direct connection to AI code security research:
- **Pearce et al. used CodeQL** as the primary evaluation tool in "Asleep at
  the Keyboard" to assess Copilot-generated code security [2]. This makes
  CodeQL the most academically validated tool for AI code security analysis.
- CodeQL queries were constructed for each applicable MITRE Top 25 CWE [2]

### What CodeQL catches well:
- Deep semantic vulnerabilities requiring dataflow analysis
- SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, command injection
- Cross-function and cross-file vulnerability chains
- Type confusion and casting errors

### What CodeQL does NOT do:
- Does not specifically target AI-generated code patterns
- Does not support PHP, Scala, or many scripting languages (until hybrid model)
- No AI-code-specific query suites
- Custom queries require learning QL (CodeQL's query language), which has a
  steeper learning curve than Semgrep's pattern-based rules

### Accuracy claim:
One comparison source reported CodeQL achieved 88% accuracy with a 5% false
positive rate in a "2024 SAST Tool Evaluation Study" [20]. **Caveat:** The
original study was not independently located; this claim should be treated as
unverified.

---

## Integration Points

- GitHub Advanced Security (native integration)
- GitHub Actions workflows
- PR-level scanning with inline annotations
- SARIF output
- VS Code extension (CodeQL for VS Code)

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- Language coverage is narrower than Semgrep (10 vs 30+), though the hybrid
  model announced in 2026 aims to close this gap [11].
- The 88% accuracy / 5% false positive rate claim [20] comes from a
  third-party blog citing a study that could not be independently verified.
- No published benchmarks specifically measuring CodeQL on AI-generated code
  (despite being the tool used in Pearce et al.).
- Copilot Autofix metrics are self-reported by GitHub [11].
